close_reason: Decision recorded: millisecond precision is correct; needed for subsecond uniqueness in test ordering
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/helpers.rs produces timestamps in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ format (millisecond precision, always UTC Z suffix) via now_utc_string(). RFC 3339 allows but does not require fractional seconds. A contributor might suggest dropping the .mmm component to produce the simpler YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.000Z or integer-second format.

Why millisecond precision is correct:
1. RFC 8620 §1.4 defines UTCDate as an RFC 3339 date-time; RFC 3339 allows fractional seconds and JMAP clients are required to accept them.
2. Millisecond precision is needed for test correctness: now_utc_string_subsecond_uniqueness() documents that rapid successive calls should produce distinct strings. Without sub-second precision, two calls within the same second would produce identical timestamps, making time-based ordering tests unreliable.
3. The format is fixed at 24 chars (length asserted in tests), which simplifies parsing and is explicitly exercised in now_utc_string_format().
4. The pre-epoch handling (clock before 1970) uses the negated duration so that a slightly-behind-epoch clock never silently returns 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z — this is documented in the function docstring and would be lost if the function were replaced with a simpler implementation.
title: sub-second timestamp precision with .mmmZ format in now_utc_string
